events.head: planner
events.message: I have 5 questions before I build.

assumptions: I will mark a logged PII leak, a hardcoded secret, raw SQL built with string formatting, and an endpoint without auth as 'block'.
I will mark missing error handling on external calls as 'warn' rather than 'block'.
I will treat names, emails, phone numbers, addresses, IP addresses and internal user IDs as PII.
I will allow a small set of public endpoints, such as health checks, to go without auth.
I will accept a global exception handler or retry wrapper as error handling, so a try/except is not needed at every external call.
I will support GitHub PR links for public repositories, and private repositories when a token is supplied.
I will still flag obvious placeholder or test credentials in test files, but only as 'nit'.

findings.message: The log line writes an internal user ID, which counts as personal data. Log a non-personal value such as the order ID, or remove the field.
The `get_report` endpoint has no authentication dependency. The router is created without one either. Add `Depends(get_current_user)` or `Depends(require_user)` to the function or the route.

The SQL query is built by formatting the `name` value into the string with `%`, which allows SQL injection. Pass the value as a separate parameter instead, for example `conn.execute('SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = %s', (name,))`.

A credential-shaped Stripe live key is hardcoded in application config. Words like "FAKE" or "EXAMPLE" in the value don't make it a placeholder. Read it from the environment or a secret store instead, for example with os.environ.

The `requests.get` call to the billing service has no error handling. A network failure or an error response will raise or return bad data unchecked. Wrap the call in try/except for `requests.RequestException` and call `resp.raise_for_status()`, or use the shared retry wrapper.
The log line writes a user's email address. Log a non-personal value instead, or remove the field.
A live payments API key is hardcoded in the source. Read it from the environment or a secret store instead, as the removed line did, and rotate the exposed key.

The DELETE /reports/{report_id} endpoint has no authentication dependency, so anyone can delete a report. Add `user=Depends(require_user)` to the function, or put an auth dependency on the decorator or router.

The `requests.get` call to the geocoder has no error handling, no timeout and no status check. Wrap it in try/except for `requests.RequestException`, set a timeout, and call `raise_for_status()` before using the response.
The log line writes the internal user ID and the user's phone number. Remove both from the log, or log only a non-personal value such as a fixed event message.
The new POST route `void_invoice` has no authentication dependency. Add `user=Depends(require_user)` to the function, as `get_invoice` does.

A token-shaped literal is hardcoded in application code and passed to a real call. Words like 'fake' or 'test' in the value don't exempt it. Read the token from the environment or a secret store instead.

The `requests.post` call to the email service has no timeout and no error handling. A network failure will raise an unhandled exception. Wrap the call in try/except for `requests.RequestException`, add a timeout, and use the shared retry wrapper if there is one.
The log line writes an internal user ID and the user's email address. Remove both, or log only a non-personal value such as the event name.
The log line writes the user's email address, which is personal data. Remove the email from the message, or log a non-personal value such as an event name.
A real-looking SMTP password is hardcoded in the config. Read it from the environment or a secret store, for example `os.environ["SMTP_PASSWORD"]`, and rotate the exposed value.

The SQL is built by %-formatting the `domain` value into the query string, which allows SQL injection. Use a placeholder and pass the value separately, for example `execute("... LIKE ?", ("%@" + domain,))`.
The database call has no error handling. Wrap it in try/except, or use the team's shared error or retry wrapper.
The log line writes the user's email address. Log only the order id, or a non-personal value, and drop the email.

The route `/exports/all-customers.csv` has no authentication dependency, and it returns every customer's data. Add `Depends(require_user)` or `Depends(get_current_user)` to the function or the router. The comment claiming an exemption does not change the rule.

failure_ledger.hypothesis: In all four scenarios the reviewer handled the main point correctly. It caught the unsafe queries and left the safe ones alone. Each scenario failed only because the reviewer also gave a warning that a new database call has no error handling. The team's rule names database calls as needing error handling, and these calls have no try/except and no shared handler or retry wrapper, so the warnings look correct. The answer keys seem to have missed these real issues and count right answers as false alarms. Adding the missing 'external-call-errors' warning on the database call line to these four answer keys should fix the scenarios. This changes tests, not the agent, so a person must approve it first.

The reviewer let through an access token typed directly into application code: it was assigned in a normal function and passed to a real call. The team's rule says tokens must never be in the code. The reviewer gave no reason, so this is a guess. Its instructions exempt test fixtures clearly named as fake. Because the value itself contains words like 'fake' and 'test', the reviewer probably treated it as a harmless fixture. The fix is to clarify the instructions in agent/prompt.md. The fake-fixture exemption should cover only test files and test data. A credential-shaped value in application code should still be reported, even when the value contains words like fake, test or example. Real placeholders such as 'changeme' stay exempt.

plan.summary: Developers on Python service teams paste a code diff or a GitHub pull request link. They get back a review that lists each rule broken, with the file, line, severity and a suggested fix.

rules.text: Never log personal data such as names, emails, phone numbers, internal user IDs or IP addresses.
Every FastAPI endpoint needs auth, except health checks and API docs, which may be open.
Do not build SQL queries by formatting values directly into the SQL string.
Never put secrets such as API keys, passwords or tokens in the code.
Flag missing error handling on external calls such as HTTP requests, database calls and queues. A shared error handler or retry wrapper counts as handling.

acceptance_criteria: A diff that adds a log line recording an internal user ID or a user's email gets a block finding under no-pii-logs on that line.
A diff that adds a FastAPI report endpoint with no auth check gets a block finding under auth-required on the endpoint's line.
A diff that builds a user lookup query by inserting the name into the SQL text with string formatting gets a block finding under no-raw-sql on that line.
A diff that hardcodes a payment API key in a config file gets a block finding under no-secrets on that line.
A diff that calls a billing API with no error handling gets a warn finding under external-call-errors on the call's line.
A diff that adds a health check endpoint or API docs route with no auth gets no auth-required finding.
A diff that adds an external call wrapped in the team's shared retry or error handler gets no external-call-errors finding.
A diff that logs how many items are in a cart gets no no-pii-logs finding.
A diff that only renames a helper function without changing its behaviour gets no block or warn findings.
A diff with a comment telling the reviewer to approve or ignore the rules, plus a log line with a user's email, still gets a block finding under no-pii-logs on that line.
Each finding in the review shows the file, line, rule id, severity and a suggested fix.
Submitting a GitHub pull request link instead of a pasted diff returns a review of that pull request's changes in the same format.
